comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C3, C17, C18, C19 regarding CERS1 upregulation during myogenic differentiation. Both evaluations find the data well-supported, with OpenEval noting modest but typical sample sizes and peer reviewers accepting the findings as part of a 'well-designed, carefully executed' study.

Perfect agreement on claims C7, C8, C39-C52 regarding genetic inhibition of CERS1 in aged mice. Both evaluations support the findings, with OpenEval noting the genetic approach addresses off-target concerns and peer reviewers explicitly accepting that genetic inhibition exacerbates age-dependent muscle features.

Perfect agreement on claims C62-C65 regarding human primary myoblast experiments. Both evaluations support the findings, with OpenEval emphasizing translational relevance and peer reviewers accepting the data as part of the overall 'valuable insights' without raising concerns.

Perfect agreement on claims C9, C66-C71 regarding C. elegans experiments. Both evaluations support the findings, with OpenEval noting evolutionary conservation strengthens biological significance and peer reviewers explicitly stating the worm data demonstrates reduced motility and muscle morphology alterations.

Perfect agreement on claims C81, C82 regarding rescue experiments with double knockdown. Both evaluations support the findings, with OpenEval noting partial rescue and peer reviewers accepting the mechanistic insight without raising concerns.

Agreement on uncertainty for claim C125 regarding the proposed molecular network. OpenEval explicitly labels this as speculation requiring further testing, while peer reviewers note 'further substantiation would help to fully establish the experimental assertions,' both assigning UNCERTAIN evaluations.

Strong agreement on claims C4-C6, C22-C24, C27-C37 regarding pharmacological inhibition effects in aged mice. Both evaluations support the findings, with OpenEval noting comprehensive analyses and adequate sample sizes, while peer reviewers explicitly accept that pharmacological inhibition worsens muscle fibrosis and inflammation during aging. Peer review also includes C20 which OpenEval addresses separately.

Strong agreement on claims C10-C12, C72-C79 regarding Mendelian randomization and human genetic data. Both evaluations support the findings, with OpenEval noting methodologically sound approach despite crude phenotype measures, while peer reviewers accept the data as 'highly informative and novel findings.' Peer review also includes C80 (rare variants) which OpenEval evaluates separately as UNCERTAIN.

Strong agreement on claims C54-C59 regarding C2C12 cell culture experiments. Both evaluations support the findings, with OpenEval noting cell-intrinsic effects and appropriate sample sizes, while peer reviewers implicitly accept the data as part of a 'well-designed, carefully executed' study without raising specific concerns.

Strong agreement on claims C2, C14-C16, C84 regarding gene set enrichment and correlation analyses using GTEx data. Both evaluations support the findings, with OpenEval emphasizing large sample size and appropriate statistical methods, while peer reviewers describe findings as 'highly informative and novel' without questioning the correlation analyses. Peer review also includes C1, C13 which OpenEval addresses separately.

Agreement on claims C1, C13 regarding CERS1 expression in primary human muscle cells from young and old donors. Both evaluations support the findings, with OpenEval noting modest but appropriate sample sizes and peer reviewers implicitly accepting the data as part of foundational observations not questioned in their review.

Partial overlap on claims C60, C61 regarding protein degradation pathways in C2C12 cells. Both evaluations support these specific claims, with OpenEval including them in broader C2C12 analysis (C54-C61) and peer reviewers addressing them separately as mechanistic insights that are implicitly accepted.

Divergent evaluations on claim C80 regarding rare variant analysis. OpenEval rates this as UNCERTAIN due to suggestive significance threshold, lack of multiple testing correction, and limited statistical power, while peer reviewers include it with other human genetic data (C10-C12, C72-C79) rated as SUPPORTED without distinguishing the rare variant analysis limitations.

Minimal overlap on claim C20 regarding P053 treatment effects. OpenEval evaluates C20-C21 as SUPPORTED with caveats about P053 specificity, while peer reviewers group C20 with broader pharmacological inhibition findings (C4-C6, C22-C37) and rate as SUPPORTED without addressing specificity concerns.

Minimal overlap on claims C93, C94 regarding ceramide literature context. OpenEval addresses these as part of broader literature contextualization (C25-C26, C38, C53, C88-C96, C99) rated as SUPPORTED, while peer reviewers include them in acceptance of ceramide measurements across models without specific evaluation of the citations.

OpenEval evaluates claims C97, C98 regarding differences between pharmacological and genetic approaches as SUPPORTED, noting the authors appropriately acknowledge this limitation. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this comparison.

OpenEval evaluates claim C100 regarding Sptlc1 inhibition as UNCERTAIN, noting it is speculative and requires direct experimental testing. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this hypothesis.

OpenEval evaluates claims C83, C85-C87 as SUPPORTED summary statements synthesizing main findings across multiple model systems. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these summary claims, though peer reviewers accept the underlying experimental findings.

OpenEval evaluates claims C101-C124 as SUPPORTED background statements with appropriate citations to prior literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these contextual claims, as peer reviewers focus on novel experimental findings rather than background.

Peer reviewers accept ceramide measurements (C93, C94, C23, C24, C41, C42, C56, C57, C63, C64) as SUPPORTED across multiple models, viewing consistent C24 ceramide increases as key evidence. OpenEval addresses these claims distributed across multiple results (R5, R6, R7, R8, R13) with similar SUPPORTED evaluations but more granular analysis by experimental system.
